source_review.notes: Reviewed the author-hosted Karger paper, Amazon Dynamo paper, primary Jump/Rendezvous/Bounded-Load/Chord papers, and official Envoy ring-hash documentation. All seven destinations returned HTTP 200. Movement and balance claims remain scoped to the stated hashing, membership, replica, and workload assumptions.

evidence: Checked ring/token/member/virtual-node/preference-list/epoch/churn/balance/handoff/fencing terminology.
Checked unsigned coordinates, `(previous,token]` ownership, equality, wrap, token/member distinction, and epoch semantics.
Checked primary placement is separated from replication, quorums, repair, transfer, consensus, and availability.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every deterministic-placement input is named as versioned protocol metadata.

evidence: Independently recomputed all eight SHA-256-derived 16-bit fixture positions.
Recomputed primary owners before/after B removal and confirmed only gamma moves B to C.
Recomputed alpha's distinct-member preference list [A,B].
Recomputed Exercise 1 equality/wrap owners and transfer of positions 11 and 25 after B removal.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Fixture arithmetic uses big-endian first-two-byte SHA-256 truncation and sorted unique tokens.

evidence: Derived insertion locality by subdivision of the successor arc.
Derived removal locality by merging the removed arc into its successor.
Reviewed expected token-share balance under independent uniform hashing and qualified finite variance.
Reviewed physical-member deduplication and topology filtering for replica preference lists.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Geometric locality is not extended to replica churn, transfer bytes, or client consistency.

evidence: Reviewed exact tokens, gaps, zero, maximum, wrap, duplicate tokens, signedness, and hash/encoding mismatch.
Reviewed one/insufficient members, repeated virtual nodes, zone shortages, weights, capacity changes, and replica churn.
Reviewed mixed/stale epochs, failed handoff, concurrent plans, flapping health, fencing, restart, rollback, and cleanup.
Reviewed Zipf/hot/adversarial keys, large objects, transfer storms, metadata bounds, and placement-hash rotation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable fixture excludes statistical balance, weights, zones, epoch transitions, handoff, quorums, failures, and persistence.

evidence: Verified sorted-token successor lookup and wrap for every fixture key.
Verified replica scanning returns distinct physical members despite virtual nodes.
Verified every changed key was owned by removed B and every prior non-B primary remains unchanged.
Verified exact ten-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The locality invariant applies only to primary owners under the identical ring snapshot except B removal.

evidence: Reviewed successor partition and insertion/removal arguments against `(previous,token]` ownership.
Reviewed probabilistic balance against independent uniform positions rather than arbitrary workloads.
Reviewed preference correctness against distinct-member and eligible-domain assumptions.
Reviewed transition outline against snapshot, replay, verification, cutover, fencing, and retention obligations.
proof_review.notes: No proof is claimed for a concrete weighted generator, failure detector, handoff protocol, quorum system, or bounded-load implementation.

evidence: Separated ring hashing, rendezvous, jump, bounded-load, centralized ranges, and DHT overlays.
Separated primary/replica churn, transfer bytes, balance dimensions, and client consistency.
The model explicitly disclaims calibrated tokens and every distributed transition/durability mechanism.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Expected/minimal movement language is never presented as universal load balance or safe migration.

evidence: The hashlib/bisect model passed exact expected output under the safe verifier.
Independent recomputation reproduced positions, owners, movement, and stability.
All seven final reference destinations returned HTTP 200.
Structure, links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippets passed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No statistical token campaign, weighted/zone replica system, handoff, failure/restart, cross-client interoperability, benchmark, or deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives ring lookup/locality, qualifies probabilistic balance, and separates physical membership, replica policy, epochs, transitions, and competing placement families.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed deterministic snapshots, weights/zones, hot keys, controlled handoff, fencing, restart, retention, snapshot validation, rate limits, and multidimensional balance/churn measurements.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review establishes placement contracts; one exact fixture anchors movement; ten examples cover mechanics and operations; five exercises span derivation, allocation, migration, and empirical choice.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/author/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external Karger, Amazon, Google, Chord, Envoy, distributed-systems, database, storage, networking, SRE, security, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither production balance, weighted placement, topology-safe replication, epoch convergence, handoff correctness, quorum behavior, failure recovery, adversarial resistance, certification, nor deployment fitness.
